title.narrative: Strengthening Governance and livelihoods in Kilimanjaro Farmers cooperatives

description.narrative: The Strengthening Governance and Livelihoods in Cooperatives (CoopGro) project is implemented by KNCU -Kilimanjaro Native Cooperative Union in four districts of the Kilimanjaro region, Tanzania. The project targets smallholder coffee farmers, who produce 90% of the region's coffee but face constraints such as weak cooperative governance, limited access to fair markets, high interest rates, low business diversification, and increasing climate-related challenges. The main purpose of the project is to enhance cooperative governance, improve livelihoods through climate-resilient practices, and promote inclusive participation in the coffee value chain. The project aims to strengthen leadership and institutional systems within cooperatives, advance climate-resilient and just food system practices, and improve access to fair and direct markets. Key activities include capacity-building trainings, hands-on field demonstrations, exchange visits, and collaborative engagements with local government and research institutions. The project directly targets 22 cooperative societies representing approximately 13,264 households and indirectly benefits about 39,702 value chain actors. Expected results include empowered and well-governed cooperatives operating transparently and democratically, improved member livelihoods, enhanced climate resilience, and stronger inclusion of women and youth in the value chain. Lessons learned will support scaling the model to other cooperatives and contribute to Tanzania's Vision 2050.
